title: Neural network experiment defense
goals: Defend a network experiment using traceable evidence
Separate selection, final evaluation and revision claims
Answer a challenge with a calculation and a bounded conclusion

prerequisite.prompt: Can a revised model reuse inspected final rows as new independent evidence?
prerequisite.answer: No. They may support regression checks, but a revised procedure needs fresh reserved cases for independent evaluation.

vocabulary: An explanation of methods and claims supported by inspectable evidence
The connection from inputs and procedure through raw outputs to a reported claim
A condition restricting what evidence can establish
Repeating the documented procedure to check reported outputs

lesson.title: Assemble a claim that can be checked

blocks.text: A defense is not a sales pitch. Assemble the original question and criterion, data roles, baseline, model equation, settings, raw checkpoints, validation selection, frozen final predictions, limitations and revision history. Someone reading the record should be able to recompute a reported MSE and see which decisions each dataset informed.

For this capstone, two rates were compared under matched conditions. Rate 0.2 selected a = 2 with validation MSE 0 versus 0.78125 for rate 0.1. The frozen candidate then achieved final MSE 5 versus baseline 20.25 on four constructed cases. These are different comparisons and must not be collapsed into “the network was 100% accurate”.

rows: Lower MSE than initial-weight baseline on these rows
Nonnegative output fails to represent negative targets
A possible representational repair, not new final evidence

blocks.title: Keep the evidence roles separate
blocks.caption: Every claim has an evidence source and a limit. A complete record is not a substitute for broader data.

blocks.text: Challenge: “Your validation error was zero, so why did the final test fail on negative targets?” Response: validation contained only positive inputs; the output max(0,a*x) cannot be negative. The final negative cases expose a coverage and architecture limitation. The overall criterion still passed, but that does not remove the failure.

Challenge: “Is a neural network better than linear regression?” Response: the supplied baseline was a fixed initial weight, not a fitted line. The evidence establishes improvement relative to that baseline only. A fitted signed line is a relevant additional comparison and needs a documented, fair evaluation. Challenge: “Was the candidate faster?” Response: no timing evidence was collected, so speed is unmeasured.

Supported case: another experiment reports baseline MSE 8 and candidate MSE 2 on four untouched final rows after freezing the candidate. The reduction is 6 MSE units, or 75% of the baseline MSE. That percentage is a relative reduction in MSE, not 75% classification accuracy. It cannot establish deployment performance.

blocks.label: Guided: calculate the absolute and relative MSE reduction, then write a sentence preserving the metric and four-row scope.

lesson.title: Close with limitations and next questions

blocks.text: Use a short presentation: question; method and controls; selection; final result; failures; revision; next question. State the small constructed sample, absent real-world coverage, limited baseline and unmeasured resource use. A useful next question is whether a signed-output procedure improves on a fitted-line baseline under newly reserved evaluation conditions. Passing this capstone means explaining the evidence correctly, including an unsuccessful or limited result.

blocks.label: Exit: correct “our network is universally reliable, 100% accurate, faster than every baseline and repaired on the final test”. Give measured claims and identify the missing evidence.

workbook.title: Build the evidence inventory
workbook.prompt: Name eight items needed to check the capstone from question through final result.
workbook.answer: Teacher explanation: Question/criterion, data and split IDs, baseline rule, architecture, initial values and learning rates, update count/loss, checkpoints and raw predictions, validation selection rule, frozen final record, limitations and revision history are acceptable items.

workbook.title: Defend the result
workbook.prompt: State the validation selection and frozen final comparison using their correct metrics and scopes.
workbook.answer: Teacher explanation: Rate 0.2 selected a = 2 with validation MSE 0 versus 0.78125 on two positive rows. Frozen final MSE was 5 versus baseline 20.25 on four constructed rows; negative-input candidate MSE was 10 on two rows.

workbook.title: Challenge an unsupported claim
workbook.prompt: A presenter claims the experiment proves neural networks beat fitted lines and use less energy. What evidence is missing?
workbook.answer: Teacher explanation: No fitted-line comparison or energy measurement was supplied. The initial-weight baseline comparison supports neither claim; specify a fair fitted-line procedure and measured resource boundary before comparing.

workbook.title: Defend a new record independently
workbook.prompt: A separate experiment compares candidates C1 and C2 on two validation rows: MSE 1.5 and 1.0. The written rule selects lower MSE. After freezing C2, four fresh final rows give baseline squared errors 4,9,1,2 and C2 squared errors 1,1,2,0. Compute final MSE and relative reduction. Two condition-B rows are the last two rows; compare baseline and candidate MSE there. State what this record supports and what is unmeasured.
workbook.answer: Teacher explanation: Select C2. Baseline final MSE 16/4 = 4; candidate MSE 4/4 = 1; absolute reduction 3 and relative reduction 75%. Condition B baseline MSE (1+2)/2 = 1.5 and candidate MSE (2+0)/2 = 1, though one condition-B row worsened from 1 to 2. The record supports lower MSE on these four final rows, not universal reliability or a classification-accuracy percentage. Speed and energy are unmeasured.

workbook.title: Record the next investigation
workbook.prompt: Propose a fair next comparison with a fitted signed line. State how to preserve previous evidence and reserve new evaluation.
workbook.answer: Teacher explanation: Keep the original plans, outputs and failures. Define and fit the signed-line baseline with development data, match task and evaluation metric, freeze both procedures, and use fresh reserved cases with positive and negative input coverage. Record revised settings and report all outcomes.

teacher.background: Use two 45-minute sessions. This capstone uses constructed scalar ReLU regression so every calculation is inspectable. It is an experiment in training and evidence, not a real-world deployment. Preserve written plans, data roles and raw predictions. Optional local Python requires no external packages or AI account. Do not expose independent-task solutions before collecting work.
materials: Printed lesson and workbook; paper and pencil
Fictional data only; reserve the independent task and fresh retry until assessment
sessions: Retrieve the prerequisite and ask students to explain the data roles.
Read section 1 and complete W1 with a recorded reason.
Trace section 2 and complete W2; compare raw values before conclusions.
Explain the diagram and complete W3 in pairs; record any support.
Complete the guided response and discuss why the evidence has limits.
Read the remaining explanation and prepare a concise experiment record.
Collect W4 independently. Require calculations and a bounded claim.
Use W5 and the exit response for feedback. Administer the fresh retry after feedback without the earlier solution.
teacher.guidedAnswer: Guided: 8 - 2 = 6 MSE units; 6/8 = 75% relative MSE reduction on four final rows. It is not classification accuracy. Exit: validation MSE 0 on two rows selected the candidate; frozen final MSE 5 versus 20.25 on four rows, with negative-output failures. Timing, stronger baselines and independent revised-model evaluation are absent.
misconceptions: A polished demonstration is an evaluation
A demonstration needs traceable data roles, metrics and raw results to support a performance claim.
Regression MSE and classification accuracy are different metrics.
A limitation bounds a result; lower error on the measured rows can be true without a universal claim.
teacher.assessment: W4 requires selection C2, MSE 4 and 1, 75% relative reduction, condition-B MSE 1.5 and 1 and recognition of the worsened row. Fresh retry: baseline squared errors 9,9,1,1; selected candidate errors 1,1,0,2. MSE 5 versus 1, relative reduction 80%; condition-B MSE both 1 with one worsened row. Require a bounded four-row conclusion.
teacher.support: Provide a frame with question, fixed settings, changed setting, data roles, raw predictions, metric, conclusion and limitation. Allow a calculator and explicit squared-error columns. Extension: implement the arithmetic locally, preserve the program version, and explain why a successful replay adds no independent test cases.
teacher.next: AI 5 begins generative and predictive objectives. Check understanding of distributions and vector similarity before advancing; provide a targeted retrieval activity where evidence is incomplete.
